segments.name: Podolia, the Cradle Nobody Can Locate

stops.name: Korolówka, the birth no register holds
stops.date_confidence: year traditional, month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January; the birthplace itself is contested across three traditions, see the two following stops. JHI gives 'Born in 1726 in Korolivka, Podolia'. No parish or communal register survives.
stops.campa: A son is born to a Sabbatean household in the Podolian countryside, and the books that would fix the day do not survive. Frankist tradition puts the birth in a village near Husiatyn with the first two years at Korolówka; the Catholic polemicist Gaudenty Pikulski, writing within Frank's own lifetime, names Buchach instead. Modern summaries settle on Korolówka. The boy is called Yaakov Leibowicz. His own account of the night, given down decades later to scribes who wrote in Polish, is not about registers at all. It is about witches around the house and a dog that would not sleep.
stops.quote: My grandmother, my mother's mother was a very learned astrologer. When I was born, all the witches assembled around our home and surrounded it, even their queen was there at their head. There was a dog in our house, a cross between a wolf and a bitch. This one did not sleep at all, but barked all the time, for if he had fallen asleep even for a moment, then they would have seen to it that he would have never awakened, but he kept watch vigilantly.
stops.quote_source: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 44, trans. Harris Lenowitz (reproduced at jacket2.org). In the printed text the dog sentence carries a dash rather than a comma and glosses the bitch as canine in brackets; the gloss is omitted here.
suggested_refs: Korolivka, Borshchiv hromada, Chortkiv Raion, Ternopil Oblast, the village the dominant birth tradition names
sources: Jewish Historical Institute, Jan Doktór, 'Jacob Frank: The Phenomenon of a Messiah' (jhi.pl)
Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank'
Harris Lenowitz, trans., The Collection of the Words of the Lord (2004), saying 44

stops.name: Buchach, the polemicist's version
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Pikulski's attribution reaches this file through secondary synthesis only; his Złość żydowska (Lwów, 1760) was not accessed directly.
stops.campa: Gaudenty Pikulski, a Bernardine friar who writes against the sect while its leader is still alive, gives Buchach as the birthplace. His Złość żydowska, printed at Lwów in 1760, is hostile testimony from close range: a man assembling evidence against Frank in the same decade Frank is standing in front of bishops. Hostile and close is not the same thing as wrong. No document has since been produced that decides between Buchach and Korolówka. The friar's own volume is scarce, and the claim now circulates only in summary.
suggested_refs: Gaudenty Pikulski, Złość żydowska przeciwko Bogu (Lwów, 1760), the earliest hostile account of the sect
sources: Dossier synthesis of Pikulski, not independently verified

stops.name: Husiatyn, the Chronicle's own claim
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The Frankist Chronicle reaches this file through Harris Lenowitz's edition as summarized in the dossier; the edition was not accessed directly, and the village it names is unnamed in the summary.
stops.campa: The Frankist Chronicle, written by believers for believers, places the birth in a village near Husiatyn and gives the child's first two years to Korolówka. Internal testimony of this kind is the worst evidence available and the only evidence of its kind: the sect keeps its own record because nobody else is keeping one for them. What the Chronicle preserves is the shape the movement wanted for its founder: a birth on the road, in a household already under suspicion, in country where the border and the confession both move. The village itself goes unnamed, in the Chronicle and in every summary of it since.
suggested_refs: Harris Lenowitz's edition of the Frankist Chronicle, the internal sectarian account of the founder's origins
sources: Dossier synthesis of the Frankist Chronicle via Lenowitz, not independently verified

stops.name: Czernowitz, the family in flight
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Czernowitz settlement (en.wikipedia: 'ca. 1730: Family moved to Czernowitz, Bukovina'); Jan Doktór separately dates the initial flight from Podolia to about 1727. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 01 January.
stops.campa: Accusations of Sabbatean heresy fall on Frank's father, and the household leaves Podolia. Bukovina is Ottoman-facing country, thin on rabbinic authority and thick with believers who kept faith with Sabbatai Zevi after his conversion to Islam. The child grows up among people whose religion is already a secret. English Wikipedia puts the family at Czernowitz around 1730; Jan Doktór dates the flight itself to about 1727, which would make the boy a year old the first time he crossed a frontier to get away from a rabbinic court.
suggested_refs: The Sabbatean communities of Bukovina and the Ottoman-Commonwealth borderland, the milieu the family fled into
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank'
Jan Doktór, reconstruction as synthesized in the dossier

stops.name: Czernowitz, the boy who declines to be taught
stops.date_confidence: inferred. No yeshiva record, attendance list, or teacher's name survives for Frank's youth; the date orders the segment and is not attested. The claim rests on the absence of any school record plus Frank's own repeated self-description.
stops.campa: No yeshiva enrolls him and no school writes his name down. He is moved among Sabbatean-influenced merchant households on the Ottoman and Commonwealth borderlands, learning roads, the languages of trade, and the doctrine that the law is finished. The ignorance he will insist on later, prostak, the simple man, the unlettered one, is a weapon he picks up and keeps sharpened for forty years. Rabbis who can quote a page against him find they are quoting it at somebody who has declined, on principle, to read it.
stops.quote: I am a prostak, I replied, and cannot make a blessing.
stops.quote_source: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 804, trans. Harris Lenowitz (jacket2.org)
suggested_refs: Frank's recurring self-description as prostak across the Words of the Lord
sources: Jan Doktór and Paweł Maciejko, as synthesized in the dossier
Harris Lenowitz, trans., The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 804

segments.name: The Frank: Ottoman Roads and the Dönmeh

stops.name: İzmir, the study with Rabbi Issohar
stops.date_confidence: stated by en.wikipedia as 1750-1752, but the evidentiary chain behind it is Frankist tradition rather than a contemporary outside record. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 01 January.
stops.campa: Smyrna is where Sabbatai Zevi was born and where the movement he broke open still keeps houses. Frank arrives in his twenties and studies, English Wikipedia says, with a Rabbi Issohar, a name later accounts attach to the lineage of Hayim Malakh. Behind the name there is very little. Here he also acquires the word that becomes his surname. Frenk, in Ottoman and Sephardi usage, is what you call a westerner, an outsider from Europe, and the Jews of Smyrna fasten it to the Ashkenazi trader up from Podolia. He carries it into a Polish cathedral and a Habsburg court as a family name.
suggested_refs: The Sabbatean houses of Smyrna, Sabbatai Zevi's birthplace, still active eighty years after the apostasy
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank' ('1750-1752: Studied in Izmir with Rabbi Issohar')
Paweł Maciejko, The Mixed Multitude (2011), as synthesized in the dossier

stops.name: Nikopol, the wedding on the Danube
stops.date_confidence: year attested (en.wikipedia and pl.wikipedia both give 1752 at Nikopol); month and day unknown, defaulted to 01 January. The bride's parentage is contradicted between the sources named in the campa and is left unresolved.
stops.campa: On the Danube, in Ottoman Bulgaria, Frank marries Chana. Polish Wikipedia gives her as the daughter of a Sabbatean rabbi; the version in wide circulation makes her the daughter of a respected Ashkenazi merchant, which is a different family and a different alliance, and the two have not been reconciled. English Wikipedia records who stood at the wedding: followers of Osman Baba. That is not a family detail. It marks the marriage as an entry into the most radical wing of the movement, the faction that held Barukhiah Russo to have been God incarnate.
suggested_refs: The Sabbatean network of the lower Danube, the setting of the 1752 marriage
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank' ('1752: Wedding witnessed by followers of Osman Baba')
Polish Wikipedia, 'Jakub Frank' ('W 1752 wziął ślub z Chaną, córką rabina sabatajskiego')

stops.name: Salonica, the Karakaş circle
stops.date_confidence: attested to November 1753 by en.wikipedia for the journey with Margalit; the specific initiation into the Karakaş faction is Frankist Chronicle tradition as reconstructed by Maciejko and Doktór, not independently corroborated. Day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He goes down to Salonica with Mordecai ben Elias Margalit and enters the Karakaş, the Dönmeh faction descended from Barukhiah Russo, dead thirty-three years and revered as Osman Baba. These are Muslims by profession and Sabbateans by conviction, an entire community living the doctrine that the messiah's apostasy was the point of the messiah. What Frank learns in Salonica is that a conversion can be a maneuver, and that a border crossed in daylight can cover a faith kept in the dark. He will practice it for the rest of his life.
stops.quote: Go lead Jacob the wise into the rooms and when you and he come to the first room, I admonish you that all the doors and gates be opened to him.
stops.quote_source: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 1, trans. Harris Lenowitz (jacket2.org); the vision is reported as set in Salonica
suggested_refs: The Karakaş or Barukhian Dönmeh of Salonica, the sect descended from Barukhiah Russo
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank' ('1753: Traveled to Salonica with Rabbi Mordechai ben Elias Margalit')
Harris Lenowitz, trans., The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 1

stops.name: Nikopol, the daughter
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The birthplace and date rest on the standard Doktór and Maciejko reconstruction of the family's itinerary; no register was located. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 01 January.
stops.campa: A daughter is born at Nikopol and named Rachel. She will be baptized Eve at Lwów, will be shown to the believers as the Virgin incarnate, will be handed the whole movement when her father dies, and will outlive him by twenty-five years and die in debt. Here in 1754 she is an infant in an Ottoman river town, in a household that is about to move north into a kingdom which will imprison her father for thirteen years. Her mother dies in that imprisonment. Eve is seventeen when it happens.
suggested_refs: The devotional portraits of Eve Frank produced by the movement, in which she is figured as the Virgin
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank'
Ada Rapoport-Albert on women in Sabbatean messianism, as synthesized in the dossier

segments.name: The Return to Podolia and the Room at Lanckoruń

stops.name: Lanckoruń, the reappearance in Podolia
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1755 for the return (en.wikipedia: 'reappeared in Podolia, gathered a group of local adherents'); no month is supported, and the pool's '1755-12' is dropped. The claim that he came under a formal Dönmeh commission is Jan Doktór's contested reconstruction, not an attested fact.
stops.campa: He is back in Podolia, and believers who kept quiet for two generations start meeting in the open. The message is not in dispute: the law given at Sinai is exhausted, and the believers are to stop pretending in front of the rabbis. English Wikipedia records only that he reappeared and gathered local adherents. Jan Doktór's reconstruction makes it a commission, the Dönmeh of Salonica sending him north with a mandate, and that framing rests on no document anyone has produced.
stops.quote: Are you Jacob the wise? I have heard that you are strong and brave-hearted.
stops.quote_source: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 1, trans. Harris Lenowitz (jacket2.org)
suggested_refs: The clandestine Sabbatean networks of Podolia, dormant since the 1690s, reactivated in 1755
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank'
Jan Doktór, reconstruction as synthesized in the dossier

stops.name: Lanckoruń, the room broken open
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1756 (en.wikipedia: 'Lanckoron/Zarichanka scandal'); early in the year per the dossier, exact month unknown and defaulted to 01 January. Lanckoruń is modern Zarichanka, Khmelnytskyi Oblast; the coordinates are the Ukrainian Wikipedia values for Zarichanka.
stops.campa: A gathering in this village is exposed and the participants are taken. The accusation, as it reaches the record, is that they danced around a woman half undressed and crowned like a Torah scroll, standing in for the Shekhinah. Everything past that point is elaboration: two centuries of retelling turn a hostile complaint into an orgy with a cast list. The arrests are real. The rabbis now have what they have wanted since Sabbatai Zevi, a sect caught in a room, and Frank, an Ottoman subject, is put over the border while his followers stay to answer for it.
suggested_refs: Zarichanka, Chemerivtsi area, Khmelnytskyi Oblast, the modern village on the site of Lanckoruń
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank'
Polish Wikipedia, 'Jakub Frank', which wikilinks Lanckorunia directly to Zariczanka

stops.name: Satanów, the tribunal and the confessions
stops.date_confidence: attested that a rabbinical court sat at Satanów following the Lanckoruń affair (en.wikipedia); the month is not given in any source reached and is set here only to order the segment after Lanckoruń.
stops.campa: A rabbinic court sits at Satanów and the people taken at Lanckoruń are questioned. Men and women confess to breaches of the Sabbath, of diet, of marriage, of the sexual law. The confessions survive. The conditions under which they were given do not. The testimony leaves the Jewish community and travels to the bishops, and the sect's own words become the material Christian authorities will use to open the next act. Whether the court heard a description of systematic rites or manufactured one under interrogation cannot be answered from the polemical record that preserved it.
suggested_refs: The Satanów depositions, the earliest body of Frankist self-description, taken under rabbinic interrogation
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank' ('Forced to leave Podolia; rabbinical court held in Satanow')

stops.name: Brody, the ban
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Reported via the rabbinic responsa tradition as synthesized by Scholem and carried in the dossier; no primary record of this specific assembly was reached, and the June dating is the tradition's, not a document's.
stops.campa: The assembly at Brody pronounces the herem. Unrepentant sectarians are cut off; communities are instructed to expose them and to deny them marriage, burial, and trade. The specific assembly comes down through the rabbinic tradition rather than through a document anyone has put on the table. Its effect is not in doubt. Excommunication forces a choice the Frankists had been avoiding, and inside a year they make it, presenting themselves to a Catholic bishop as Contra-Talmudists persecuted by the Talmud.
suggested_refs: The Brody herem of 1756 against the Sabbatean sectarians of Podolia
sources: Gershom Scholem's Sabbatean studies, as synthesized in the dossier; not independently verified

stops.name: Kamieniec Podolski, the bishop's tribunal
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1757 by the Jewish Historical Institute ('Participated in public disputes with rabbis in Kamieniec Podolski'); the month is not specified in any source reached and is set here only to order the segment before the October burning order.
stops.campa: Bishop Mikołaj Dembowski takes up the sect's petition and stages a disputation in his episcopal city. The Frankists appear as Contra-Talmudists: they accept the Zohar, they reject the Talmud, they profess a triune Godhead, and they ask the Church for protection against the rabbis. It is a position assembled to be legible to a bishop, and it works. Dembowski rules for them. What no record recovers is how much of the theology the disputants held and how much of it was the shape a Polish bishop needed to see before he would act.
suggested_refs: The 1757 Kamieniec disputation acts, the first Frankist self-presentation to a Catholic tribunal
sources: Jewish Historical Institute, Jan Doktór, 'Jacob Frank: The Phenomenon of a Messiah' (jhi.pl)

stops.name: Kamieniec Podolski, the Talmud burned
stops.date_confidence: the burning order following the Kamieniec ruling is attested and dated 17 October 1757 in the dossier chronology; the burnings themselves are recorded without a day-level count of copies.
stops.campa: The bishop orders copies of the Talmud collected and burned in public. Wagons are emptied into the fire, and the Jewish communities of Podolia lose books that cost a lifetime's wages to buy. The Frankists have won their ruling by supplying a Christian authority with Jewish witnesses against Jewish books. Nothing else in Frank's career costs the people he came from as much, and nothing else in it is as hard to read as a purely tactical move. The order carries the date of the seventeenth of October.
suggested_refs: The 1757 Talmud burnings in Podolia, ordered on the strength of the Kamieniec ruling
sources: Jewish Historical Institute (jhi.pl)
Dossier chronology, 17 October 1757 burning order

stops.name: Kamieniec Podolski, the bishop dead
stops.date_confidence: attested: pl.wikipedia, 'Mikołaj Dembowski', gives 17 November 1757 at Czarnokozińce near Kamieniec. The pin is Kamieniec Podolski itself because no coordinate for Czarnokozińce was located; the death did not occur in the city. The reading of the death as divine judgment is legend, not fact.
stops.campa: One month after the burning order Dembowski dies, at Czarnokozińce outside the city, with the archbishopric of Lwów already conferred on him by Augustus III and never taken up. Jewish Podolia reads the death as a judgment and goes on saying so for generations. The death is documented; the providence is not, and the two travel together through every retelling. For the Frankists it is a plain disaster. Their protector is gone and the ruling stands with nobody to enforce it. The rabbis come back at them inside the year, holding the civil power that had been held off.
suggested_refs: Czarnokozińce, near Kamieniec Podolski, where Dembowski died on 17 November 1757
sources: Polish Wikipedia, 'Mikołaj Dembowski'
Gershom Scholem and Jan Doktór, on the providential reading, as synthesized in the dossier

stops.name: Iwanie, the fourth company
stops.date_confidence: the dossier places the Iwanie period 1757-1759; en.wikipedia's 'Frankism' names Ivanie as one of four company locations. No month is attested; June 1758 is set to order the segment. Whether Frank declared himself messiah here or followers assigned him the role is disputed and unresolved.
stops.campa: At Iwanie, one of four company centers the movement recognizes, Frank tells the believers that a new stage has opened. He is treated here as what comes after Sabbatai Zevi and after Barukhiah Russo, the third in a line. Whether he declares it or they assign it to him is not recoverable from anything that survives. The camp is a household and a doctrine at once: they live together, share what they have, and prepare for the baptism that is coming. English Wikipedia names Iwanie alongside Częstochowa, Brno, and Offenbach as the four.
stops.quote_source: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 451, trans. Harris Lenowitz (jacket2.org)
suggested_refs: Ivane-Puste, Chortkiv Raion, Ternopil Oblast, the modern village on the site of Iwanie
sources: Wikipedia, 'Frankism' ('There were four company locations, in Ivanie, Częstochowa, Brno, and Offenbach am Main')
Harris Lenowitz, trans., The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 451

stops.name: Lwów, the second disputation
stops.date_confidence: attested: de.wikipedia gives 'Am 17. Juli 1759 startete in der Lateinischen Kathedrale zu Lemberg die Zweite Disputation', running to 19 September. The Jewish Historical Institute article, sometimes cited for this, does not name Lwów and is not the authority for the venue.
stops.campa: In the Latin cathedral at Lwów the Frankists face the rabbis a second time, from the seventeenth of July into September. The propositions go further than Kamieniec did: alongside the anti-Talmudic articles they advance the blood accusation, that Jews use Christian blood. It is untrue, it is advanced by Jews against Jews, and some historians argue the Church required it as the price of protection, which explains the move without excusing it. The rabbis who come to answer are answering a charge that can end their communities.
suggested_refs: The Latin Archcathedral of the Assumption, Lviv, site of the July to September 1759 disputation
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Jakob Joseph Frank'
Paweł Maciejko, The Mixed Multitude, on the 17 July to 19 September dates, as synthesized in the dossier

stops.name: Lwów, the font in the cathedral
stops.date_confidence: attested (en.wikipedia: 'September 17, 1759: Baptized in Lwow; baptismal name Joseph'). The size of the accompanying baptism wave is disputed: JHI gives approximately 2,000, Doktór about 2,000, Maciejko 3,000 to 4,000.
stops.campa: On the seventeenth of September Frank is baptized in the cathedral where the disputation was held, and takes the name Józef. Anna Brühl and Franciszek Rzewuski stand as godparents. Around two thousand of his followers are baptized in the same wave by the Jewish Historical Institute's count, and other reconstructions run to three or four thousand. The Polish nobility acquires several thousand new Catholics of Jewish origin inside a single season, and Frank acquires a legal existence in a Christian kingdom. He is thirty-three years old and has been in Poland four years.
stops.quote: Come, I will show you a tasty comedy, how a man is rolling in the dirt and a priest praying to him.
stops.quote_source: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 793, trans. Harris Lenowitz (jacket2.org)
suggested_refs: The 1759 baptismal registers of the Lwów archdiocese, recording the mass conversion of the Contra-Talmudists
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank'
Jewish Historical Institute (jhi.pl), 'Approximately 2,000 followers were baptized in 1759'
Harris Lenowitz, trans., The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 793

stops.name: Warsaw, the king stands godfather
stops.date_confidence: 18 November 1759 at the Saxon Palace, supported independently by pl.wikipedia ('18 Listopada... Józef Frank przyjął chrzest... w pałacu Saskim') and by Maciejko's archival dating. En.wikipedia's 'baptized again the next day', 18 September, is the outlier and is treated here as an error. The pin is the canonical atlas Warsaw coordinate; the Saxon Palace's own coordinate is 52.2411, 21.0114, some two hundred metres off.
stops.campa: In the chapel of the Saxon Palace Frank is baptized a second time, with more ceremony, and Augustus III of Poland stands as godfather. English Wikipedia dates this to the day after Lwów; Polish scholarship and Paweł Maciejko's archival work both give the eighteenth of November, two months later, and the documents support the interval. A king of Poland has now sponsored at the font a man the rabbis of Podolia excommunicated three years earlier. The court believes it has acquired a missionary.
stops.quote: Some new road is prepared for me.
stops.quote_source: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 793, trans. Harris Lenowitz (jacket2.org)
suggested_refs: The chapel of the Saxon Palace, Warsaw, destroyed in 1944; the site is now Piłsudski Square
sources: Polish Wikipedia, 'Jakub Frank'
Paweł Maciejko, The Mixed Multitude, as synthesized in the dossier
Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank', for the contradicted September dating

segments.name: Thirteen Years Under the Black Madonna

stops.name: Warsaw, the arrest in the Bernardine church
stops.date_confidence: contested by one day: en.wikipedia gives 6 February 1760, de.wikipedia 7 February, at the church of the Warsaw Bernardine monastery. The 6th is used to order the file and the discrepancy is not resolved. He was handed to the Inquisition on 13 February 1760. The pin is the Bernardine church on Krakowskie Przedmieście, not the generic city coordinate.
stops.campa: Four months after the royal baptism he is taken in the church of the Warsaw Bernardine convent. English Wikipedia dates the arrest to the sixth of February, German Wikipedia to the seventh. The charge is that the conversion was a covering, that the baptized Contra-Talmudists are still one sect under one master, and that the master is being addressed as something other than a man, which is an accurate account of what his people believe. He is held with the Camaldolese and handed to the Inquisition on the thirteenth.
suggested_refs: The church of the Warsaw Bernardine monastery, Krakowskie Przedmieście, site of the February 1760 arrest
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Jakob Joseph Frank'
Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank' ('February 6, 1760: Arrested in Warsaw for heresy')

stops.name: Jasna Góra, the fortress of the Black Madonna
stops.date_confidence: attested for the fact and the span (Wikipedia, 'Jasna Góra Monastery': 'Between 1760 and 1772 in the monastery was imprisoned Jacob Frank'); the month of transfer is not given and March is set only to order the segment after the February arrest.
stops.campa: He is sent to the Pauline monastery at Częstochowa, a fortified house on a hill holding the most venerated image in Poland. The sentence is ecclesiastical confinement rather than a dungeon: he is inside the walls, under the Black Madonna, for what becomes thirteen years. The Paulines have shut a heresiarch up inside the national shrine, and by doing it they have given his movement a fixed address. Wikipedia's article on the monastery records the imprisonment plainly and calls him a man who considered himself a messiah.
stops.quote: Be what may, I will go with God's help
stops.quote_source: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 1, trans. Harris Lenowitz (jacket2.org)
suggested_refs: The Jasna Góra monastery and the icon of the Black Madonna of Częstochowa
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jasna Góra Monastery'
Jewish Historical Institute (jhi.pl)

stops.name: Jasna Góra, the court inside the walls
stops.date_confidence: inferred. That the confinement was porous and that Frank directed the movement through visitors and letters is attested in general terms by JHI and the dossier; the 1765 date is a midpoint chosen to order the segment and marks no event.
stops.campa: The confinement leaks. Family come, disciples come, letters go out and money comes in, and the movement is run from inside a monastery for over a decade. The imprisonment turns into the founding ordeal of the sect: their master shut up in the fortress of the Virgin, at the dead center of Catholic Poland, and the doctrine reorganizes itself around the fact. Frankism after 1760 is a religion with a prison at the middle of it. Believers make the journey from Podolia and Moravia to stand under the walls.
suggested_refs: The Pauline monastery precinct at Częstochowa, functioning from 1760 as the movement's institutional center
sources: Jewish Historical Institute (jhi.pl)
Wikipedia, 'Frankism'

stops.name: Jasna Góra, Chana dead
stops.date_confidence: circa 1771. De.wikipedia dates the death two years before the release of January 1773; no civil death record was located, and the month is unknown and defaulted to 01 January. The burial in the cave systems near Olsztyn is de.wikipedia's.
stops.campa: Chana dies inside the confinement, about two years before the release, and German Wikipedia reports her buried in the cave systems near Olsztyn rather than in any churchyard. No civil death record has been located. Her daughter is seventeen. From here Eve moves to the center of the movement's devotion, addressed and painted as the Virgin, standing where her mother stood as wife and standing also where the Catholic imagery all around them puts the Mother of God.
suggested_refs: The caves near Olsztyn, Częstochowa county, reported burial place of Chana Frank
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Jakob Joseph Frank'
Ada Rapoport-Albert on women in Sabbatean messianism, as synthesized in the dossier

stops.name: Jasna Góra, the Russians open the gate
stops.date_confidence: 21 January 1773, attested by de.wikipedia ('am 21. Januar 1773 frei') and supported by pl.wikipedia's 1773. En.wikipedia's 'August 1772' is the outlier. General Bibikov is named only by en.wikipedia; his own article mentions neither Częstochowa nor Frank, and the attribution is not carried here as fact.
stops.campa: Russian forces holding Częstochowa during the suppression of the Bar Confederation release Frank and his daughter on the twenty-first of January. English Wikipedia dates it to August 1772 and credits General Bibikov, whose own biography mentions neither the town nor the prisoner; German and Polish sources both give 1773. His Polish sentence is never annulled. Offenbach lore will later claim the release paid for espionage on the tsar's behalf. No ledger or commission has ever been produced for it.
suggested_refs: The Russian occupation of Częstochowa during the Bar Confederation, 1772-1773
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Jakob Joseph Frank'
Polish Wikipedia, 'Jakub Frank'
Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank', for the contradicted August 1772 dating

segments.name: Brno: the Court of the Baron

stops.name: Warsaw, the merchant's retinue
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The Warsaw stopover and the disguise as a merchant's servants come from the Frankist chronology as synthesized in the dossier; no Polish administrative record was located. February 1773 is set to order the segment between the release and the Brno arrival.
stops.campa: He passes back through Warsaw, briefly, on his way out of the country that held him. The stopover is reported by the Frankist chronology rather than by any Polish record. He entered Poland in 1755 as an Ottoman subject preaching against the rabbis, and leaves it eighteen years later a baptized Catholic with an unspent monastery sentence behind him. What goes out of Warsaw toward Moravia is a party of some eighteen people got up as the servants of a rich merchant, with Frank and Eve inside it.
suggested_refs: The Frankist Chronicle's account of the 1773 departure from Poland
sources: Dossier chronology synthesis of Maciejko and Doktór; not independently verified

stops.name: Brno, the Dobruška house
stops.date_confidence: March 1773 for the arrival is Frankist Chronicle tradition per the dossier; en.wikipedia gives the Brno residence as 1772-1786. The Dobruška kinship and Moses Dobruška's own dates are attested by en.wikipedia, 'Moses Dobruška'.
stops.campa: In Brno he is taken in by the Dobruškas, wealthy, Sabbatean-connected, and related to him: Schöndl Dobruška, born Hirschel, is his first cousin. Her son Moses, twenty years old, will convert in 1775, be ennobled at Vienna in 1778 as Franz Thomas Edler von Schönfeld, join the Asiatic Brethren and the Illuminati, go to Paris in 1792 as Junius Frey, and be guillotined in 1794. Whatever passes out of this household into European Freemasonry passes through the cousin's son, not through Frank, who joins no lodge and no order.
suggested_refs: Moses Dobruška, later Franz Thomas von Schönfeld and Junius Frey, guillotined 5 April 1794
sources: Wikipedia, 'Moses Dobruschka' (birth 12 July 1753, conversion 17 December 1775, ennoblement 25 July 1778, execution 5 April 1794)
Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank' ('1772-1786: Lived in Brno, Moravia')

stops.name: Brno, the Uhlans and the pilgrims
stops.date_confidence: the court structure is corroborated across secondary sources and Habsburg police and diplomatic material as synthesized in the dossier; no financial accounts are extant. 1775 is a midpoint set to order the segment and marks no single event.
stops.campa: The court takes shape: uniformed guards his people call Uhlans, attendants under discipline, a household run on the etiquette of a small sovereign. Money arrives from believers in Poland and Moravia, and pilgrims arrive behind the money. A man who came out of a Polish monastery two years ago now keeps a guard at his door, and nobody in Brno can say what religion is practiced behind it. No account books survive, so the scale is known only from what Habsburg officials and neighbors wrote down about what they were looking at.
suggested_refs: Habsburg police and diplomatic reports on the Brno court, the basis of Maciejko's archival reconstruction
sources: Paweł Maciejko, The Mixed Multitude, as synthesized in the dossier
Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank'

stops.name: Brno, Goliński's denunciation
stops.date_confidence: the 1776 Austrian inquiry opened after the former follower Goliński's denunciation is described on pl.wikipedia in its entry on the film Daas; the month is unknown and defaulted to 01 January. The dossier's earlier placement of this episode in Vienna at a Stephansplatz pin is dropped as an arbitrary coordinate for an administrative proceeding.
stops.campa: A former follower named Jakub Goliński goes to the Austrian authorities. Frank has taken his wife and will not give her back, and the household holds a power over its members that the state ought to look into. An inquiry opens in 1776, the first time the court is examined as a police matter rather than admired as a curiosity. The file it starts is the file that eventually turns Frank out of Moravia. Polish Wikipedia carries the episode in its entry on the film made of it.
suggested_refs: The 1776 Austrian inquiry into the Brno court, dramatized in Adrian Panek's film Daas (2011)
sources: Polish Wikipedia, entry on the film Daas
Paweł Maciejko's archival research, as synthesized in the dossier

stops.name: Vienna, the audiences at the Hofburg
stops.date_confidence: attested that Frank visited Vienna repeatedly and gained the favour of Maria Theresa and Joseph II (en.wikipedia); no dated audience was located, and June 1777 is set only to order the segment. Stories of closer imperial intimacy, including a joint visit by Joseph II and the future Paul I of Russia, exceed the documentation.
stops.campa: Frank and Eve travel repeatedly to Vienna, and English Wikipedia records that Maria Theresa and Joseph II received them with interest, the empress apparently seeing a man who might bring Jews to the Church in quantity. Stories of a closer intimacy circulate, including a joint visit by Joseph II and the future Paul of Russia, and they run well past anything documented. The audiences themselves are credible enough. He is a baptized Catholic with a following and no country of his own. No dated audience has been located in any record reached.
suggested_refs: The Hofburg under Maria Theresa and Joseph II, the setting of Frank's Vienna audiences
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank' ('Visited Vienna multiple times; gained favor of Maria Theresa and Joseph II')

stops.name: Brno, the words taken down
stops.date_confidence: attested: saying 804 carries the date line 'The Lord saw a dream the 14th of June 1784' in the manuscript as translated by Lenowitz. The sayings as a whole were recorded across 1784 and 1789-1790, in Brno and then Offenbach.
stops.campa: Scribes write the sayings down as he gives them, in Polish, in the register of a man recounting dreams to a household: the sick night at Dziurdziów, the woman with the well of living water, the dead who come asking to be sent on a mission. The collection will run past two thousand numbered sayings. He is not writing scripture and does not pretend to be. What survives of his mind survives because a court with nothing else to do wrote it out. On the fourteenth of June 1784 a scribe heads the entry with the date and takes down a dream.
stops.quote: The Lord saw a dream the 14th of June 1784: Two women came to me, and one man 6 cubits tall. They were very beautiful, and they said to me, We have heard in the place where we live that your people have abandoned you and that you do not want to send them on any mission. We have been dead several thousand years and we have worked a lot, and still we have no peace. We ask you, Send us. We will go on your mission wholeheartedly.
stops.quote_source: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 804, trans. Harris Lenowitz (jacket2.org). The saying continues past this point: they ask whether he blesses his people, hand him a book written in large Hebrew letters without dots, and he raises his hands over their heads and blesses them.
suggested_refs: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, recorded by Frank's scribes from 1784
sources: Harris Lenowitz, trans., The Collection of the Words of the Lord (2004), saying 804

stops.name: Brno, the wisdom of sorcery
stops.date_confidence: the saying is undated in the sources reached; 1785 is set only to order the segment inside the Brno years. Saying 868 is attested in the Lenowitz translation.
stops.campa: He tells them their education was the wrong one. The learning he keeps recommending is neither Talmud nor catechism; it is the practical wisdom the rabbis anathematized and the Church burned people over, and it belongs to the same argument as his refusal to read. A man who calls himself a prostak in one saying tells his followers in another that they ought to have been taught sorcery. Both statements do identical work. They put him outside the two literacies that could otherwise be used to test him.
stops.quote: It would be better for you if you had been taught the wisdom of sorcery; you would have known a great deal.
stops.quote_source: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 868, trans. Harris Lenowitz (jacket2.org)
suggested_refs: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, sayings 804 and 868, on learning and unlearning
sources: Harris Lenowitz, trans., The Collection of the Words of the Lord, sayings 804 and 868

segments.name: Offenbach: the House by the Main

stops.name: Brno, the toleration ends
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1786 for the departure (en.wikipedia, 'Left Brno'); no month is given and 01 January is the default. The Goliński complaint is attached as cause by the dossier's synthesis of Habsburg police records rather than by a single cited order.
stops.campa: Habsburg patience runs out. The Goliński complaint, the armed look of the guard, money moving in from abroad, and a sect that will not resolve into any recognized confession add up to a foreign body the administration no longer wants sitting inside Moravia. One state has imprisoned him and a second has now expelled him. He moves west with a household of several hundred people and no invitation waiting anywhere. English Wikipedia records only that he left Brno in 1786, when he was sixty.
suggested_refs: Habsburg police files on the Brno court, 1776-1786
sources: Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank' ('1786: Left Brno')
Dossier synthesis of Habsburg police records

stops.name: Oberrad, the waiting house
stops.date_confidence: attested by the city of Offenbach's own history page ('Frank and his entourage initially stayed in Oberrad while renovations were completed'); no month is given and June 1786 is set to order the segment between Brno and Offenbach.
stops.campa: The party stops at Oberrad, a village outside Frankfurt, while a residence is made ready downriver. The city of Offenbach's own historical account puts it plainly: Frank and his entourage stayed here while renovations were finished. What that means on the ground is a court of several hundred people parked in a Hessian village, paying for lodging and waiting on plasterers. No month is given for the arrival and no source says how long the wait ran. The Main is two miles off.
suggested_refs: Oberrad, now a district of Frankfurt am Main, the staging point for the move to Offenbach
sources: City of Offenbach, 'Die Frankisten' (offenbach.de)

stops.name: Offenbach, the Isenburg castle
stops.date_confidence: three sources give three dates: de.wikipedia, following the Frankist Chronicle, gives 3 March 1787 with fifty to eighty followers; pl.wikipedia gives March 1786; offenbach.de gives 1788. The most specific is used to order the file and the conflict is not resolved. The name 'Gottes Haus' appears on none of the pages checked and is not carried here.
stops.campa: Prince Wolfgang Ernst II of Isenburg-Birstein, short of money, lets his Renaissance castle on the Main to the newcomer. The dates do not agree with each other: German Wikipedia, following the Frankist Chronicle, gives the third of March 1787 with fifty to eighty followers; Polish Wikipedia says March 1786; the city of Offenbach says 1788. Into a town of about five thousand people come baptized Jews from Poland, Moravia and Bohemia, with a uniformed guard behind them. Frank signs himself Baron of Offenbach.
suggested_refs: The Isenburger Schloss, Offenbach am Main, leased from Wolfgang Ernst II of Isenburg-Birstein
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Jakob Joseph Frank'
Polish Wikipedia, 'Jakub Frank'
City of Offenbach, 'Die Frankisten' (offenbach.de)
Jewish Encyclopedia (1906), 'Offenbach' ('Frank, assuming the title of Baron of Offenbach, kept his court')

stops.name: Offenbach, the Pollakengarten
stops.date_confidence: attested that older Offenbach city maps carry the name Pollakengarten on the Rosenhöhe (offenbach.de); the coordinates are an approximate placement on the Rosenhöhe area, since no historical plot boundary was recoverable. The date orders the segment and marks no event.
stops.campa: On the rise the town later calls the Rosenhöhe, older Offenbach maps carry a plot named the Pollakengarten, the garden of the Poles. Nobody in Offenbach is told what the household believes. What the residents see is an eastern prince with soldiers, a daughter kept like a princess, and money, three million gulden by the municipal account, arriving from a source none of them can trace. Frank's guards camp on the plot, drill there, and hold their celebrations there, and the name is what the town has left of them.
suggested_refs: The Rosenhöhe at Offenbach am Main, shown on older city maps as the Pollakengarten
sources: City of Offenbach, 'Die Frankisten' (offenbach.de)

stops.name: Offenbach, the dream of the spring
stops.date_confidence: saying 504 is undated within the collection; the dream-visions of this kind are placed by the dossier in 1784 and 1789-1790. 1790 is set to order the segment inside the Offenbach years.
stops.campa: The dreams recorded at Offenbach come at the end of a life spent crossing between religions, and Jesus turns up inside them, seated at a spring of living and clear water with priests around him. This is not the imagery of a man performing Catholicism for a Polish court. It is the imagery of the doctrine he has held since Salonica, in which the messiah's descent through the other faiths is the work itself. The water at the middle of the dream is the same water the woman offered him in the field at Dziurdziów, forty years back.
stops.quote: In a dream I saw Jesus, having priests around him, sitting at a spring of living and clear water.
stops.quote_source: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, saying 504, trans. Harris Lenowitz (jacket2.org)
suggested_refs: The Collection of the Words of the Lord, sayings 2 and 504, the well of living water and the spring
sources: Harris Lenowitz, trans., The Collection of the Words of the Lord, sayings 2 and 504

stops.name: Offenbach, four in the morning
stops.date_confidence: attested. The date is agreed across en.wikipedia, de.wikipedia, JHI, and offenbach.de. The hour differs slightly: JHI gives 4 a.m., de.wikipedia about 4:30. The cause, a stroke, is given independently by de.wikipedia ('an einem Schlaganfall') and offenbach.de.
stops.campa: He dies in the castle at about four in the morning, of a stroke by the account of both the city of Offenbach and German Wikipedia. The Jewish Historical Institute gives the hour as four, German Wikipedia as half past. His followers had understood him to promise that he would not die, or that his death would not be the ordinary kind, and several hundred of them are living in the town on the strength of that understanding. The news goes around the building before dawn. He is sixty-five.
suggested_refs: The Isenburger Schloss at Offenbach, where Frank died on 10 December 1791
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Jakob Joseph Frank'
City of Offenbach, 'Die Frankisten' (offenbach.de)
Jewish Historical Institute (jhi.pl)
Wikipedia, 'Jacob Frank'

stops.name: Offenbach, the funeral without a priest
stops.date_confidence: attested by de.wikipedia for the date and the detail; the city of Offenbach's own history page describes the same funeral in near-identical terms. The coordinates are those of Wilhelmsplatz, built over the former municipal cemetery.
stops.campa: Two days later they bury him in the municipal cemetery. Bells are rung. There is no priest and no Christian rite, and the Church that baptized him twice and imprisoned him once is not represented at the graveside. A town of five thousand watches a foreign army bury its king in the town's own churchyard. Around eight hundred Frankists walk in procession at a reported cost of ten thousand guilders, the women in white, the bodyguards carrying rifles, the officers with sabres drawn.
suggested_refs: The former municipal cemetery of Offenbach am Main, now Wilhelmsplatz
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Jakob Joseph Frank'

segments.name: What Was Left in the Ground

stops.name: Offenbach, the green marks on the grave
stops.date_confidence: attested for the practice by de.wikipedia, which dates it across the period from the burial to the 1866 clearance; 1800 is a midpoint set to order the segment and marks no single event.
stops.campa: Followers keep coming to the grave, and to Eve's beside it after 1816, and they mark the spots with green paint applied where it will not be noticed. Green is the Sabbatean colour of reverence. A Catholic burial ground in a Hessian town is being used as a pilgrimage site by people who appear on the parish books as Christians, and the marks are hidden because the practice cannot be admitted to. There is no synagogue in this and no church in it either. The visits go on for three quarters of a century.
suggested_refs: The concealed green markers on the Frank family graves, Offenbach
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Jakob Joseph Frank' and 'Wilhelmsplatz (Offenbach am Main)'
Jewish Encyclopedia (1906), 'Offenbach', on the tomb as a pilgrimage site

stops.name: Offenbach, the lease comes apart
stops.date_confidence: Eve Frank's death is attested to 7 September 1816 by de.wikipedia, preceded by a March 1816 Hofgericht attachment of her and her estate at a Mainz creditor's instance. The pool's '1816/1817' hedge is dropped. The reported deaths of Joseph in 1807 and Roch in 1813 could not be verified in any source reached.
stops.campa: The court Frank leased into being runs on after him for twenty-five years and then stops. In March 1816 the Hofgericht attaches Eve and her whole estate at the instance of a Mainz creditor; on the seventh of September she is dead. Her brothers Joseph and Roch are reported dead in 1807 and 1813 without heirs, though nothing reached confirms it. A rumour goes round Offenbach that she did not die at all, that an Isenburg court official got her out of the city. Two independent sources record the rumour. Neither treats it as history.
suggested_refs: The 1816 Hofgericht attachment of Eve Frank's estate at a Mainz creditor's instance
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Jakob Joseph Frank'
Jewish Encyclopedia (1906), 'Offenbach' (Eve 'either was spirited away or died suddenly')

stops.name: Offenbach, the cemetery leveled and the skull taken
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1866 for the clearance and the removal of the skull (de.wikipedia, corroborated by Kraushar's bibliography citing Emil Pirazzi, Bilder aus Offenbach's Vergangenheit, 1879); the month is unknown. Kraushar's photograph dates to his 1894 research trip. The chain of custody after Pirazzi is not established anywhere.
stops.campa: The old municipal cemetery is cleared and leveled, and workmen open the Frank family graves. Emil Pirazzi, a local historian, takes Jacob Frank's skull out of the ground and keeps it on a shelf in his house, where the Polish historian Aleksander Kraushar photographs it in 1894 while researching what becomes the standard prewar biography. After Pirazzi the chain of custody stops. No modern identification of the object has been made, and nobody has recorded where it went.
suggested_refs: Emil Pirazzi, Bilder aus Offenbach's Vergangenheit (1879); Aleksander Kraushar's 1894 photograph of the skull
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Jakob Joseph Frank'
Aleksander Kraushar, Frank i frankiści polscy (1895), vol. 3, via archive.org OCR

stops.name: Warsaw, the last complete manuscript burns
stops.date_confidence: en.wikipedia's 'Frankism' states that the last known complete manuscript, sayings 1 to 2192, was destroyed with numerous other Frankist sources in the destruction of Warsaw in the Second World War. The August 1944 date orders the stop against the Warsaw Uprising and is not given by the source; the exact date and circumstance are unknown.
stops.campa: The Words of the Lord ran to two thousand one hundred and ninety-two numbered sayings in its last complete copy, and that copy goes with much else of the Frankist paper in the destruction of Warsaw. What Frank said out loud to a room in Brno and Offenbach now exists as a reconstruction with holes in it. Partial witnesses survive at the Jagiellonian in Kraków and in the Lublin public library, and it is on those that Jan Doktór's Polish critical edition and Harris Lenowitz's English translation of 2004 are built.
suggested_refs: Jagiellonian Library mss. 6968 and 6969/1-3; Lublin Public Library ms. 2118, the surviving partial witnesses
sources: Wikipedia, 'Frankism'
Dossier manuscript census (Jagiellonian and Lublin holdings)
Harris Lenowitz, The Collection of the Words of the Lord (2004); Stanford SearchWorks record

stops.name: Wilhelmsplatz, the vaults under the square
stops.date_confidence: attested to the 2009-2011 renovation of Wilhelmsplatz (de.wikipedia, 'Wilhelmsplatz (Offenbach am Main)'); mid-2010 is set to order the stop within that span and is not a documented date.
stops.campa: Offenbach renovates the square built over the old cemetery, and the crews find three masonry-vaulted burial chambers a metre and a quarter down. The remains are moved to the current municipal cemetery. No plaque goes up. The city's own history page tells the funeral in full detail, the white dresses and the drawn sabres and the bells, and says nothing at all about where the man is now. He is under a square in Offenbach, or he was until 2011, and nothing above ground says so.
suggested_refs: Wilhelmsplatz, Offenbach am Main, renovated 2009-2011, unmarked
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Wilhelmsplatz (Offenbach am Main)'
